subject: Contingency activation latency & redundancy scope amendment
messages:
From: Kelsey Martin <ops@nimbuspay.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@nimbuspay.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Contingency activation latency & redundancy scope amendment

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the dedicated capacity numbers look promising. As we start mapping our regulatory continuity requirements, a couple of constraints popped up on our side that may require a concession to Redwood's standard multi-region failover SLA.

Short version: our compliance team requires an RTO of 2 hours and RPO of 4 hours for the payments clearing service in the US region when an entire primary region becomes unavailable. We understand Redwood's standard policy is tighter for hosted tiers, but our platform cannot tolerate full dual-active replication for cost reasons.

Can Redwood consider a scoped amendment that: 
- treats Nimbus as warm-standby (cross-region cold-activation) for the payments-clearing namespace,
- guarantees activation lead time not to exceed 120 minutes (RTO) with data recovery to within 4 hours (RPO), and
- codifies a limited liability exposure for cross-region activation windows tied to our planned maintenance blackout windows.

We can provide runbooks and a short DR playbook for the specific service to accelerate validation. If you need, I can loop in legal/procurement. Ideally we'd have a redline to present to our auditors by 24 Mar.

Attachments: runbook_v1.txt (stub) referenced in body; I can share a formal runbook if helpful.

Thanks,
Kelsey Martin
Head of Ops, Nimbus Payments
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Kelsey Martin <ops@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contingency activation latency & redundancy scope amendment

Kelsey — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. I looped in Marissa (customer success / renewals) and Hannah (SRE & product ops) so we can scope this quickly. A few quick clarifying questions before we draft an amendment: 

1) Is the RTO/RPO requirement limited to the single "payments-clearing" namespace or does it include adjacent services (auth, ledger-ingest)?
2) Do you expect any traffic shaping or planned traffic drain prior to activation (i.e., do you want us to pause incoming requests or accept degraded throughput during the window)?
3) Was your preference for a contractual carveout (amendment to standard SLA) or an operational runbook + attestation? Auditors often want contractual language.

From our side, a warm-standby carveout is plausible if we: (a) agree on a deterministic activation checklist, (b) accept a documented RTO of up to 120 minutes for that namespace, and (c) limit the scope of regional liability (we typically cap availability credits in carveouts). Hannah, can you sketch the activation steps and the major risks we need to document?

I'll start a draft amendment and share a draft by EOD Wednesday (17 Mar). Does that timing work for you?

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Contingency activation latency & redundancy scope amendment — request for approval

Aditya — forwarding a request from Nimbus Payments. High level: they need a scoped SLA amendment to allow warm-standby activation for a single critical namespace with RTO=120m / RPO=4h. They asked for a contractual redline by 24 Mar for audit review.

Key commercial tradeoffs: 
- Revenue: mid-six-figure ARR (expansion motion); precedent: we haven't granted legal carveouts with RTO this lenient for hosted tenants at scale.
- Operational: Hannah believes technical plan is straightforward but needs explicit activation lead time, runbook attachments, and a scheduled DR test calendar.
- Risk: We should limit long-term liability (credits/termination triggers) and add a clause requiring Nimbus to follow the agreed runbook and share post-activation RCA within 5 business days.

My recommendation: approve a scoped amendment for this account with the following guardrails — 12-month term pilot, quarterly DR tests, liability cap = one month of committed spend, and documented runbook as an invoice-able setup fee. This gives them auditor coverage while protecting Redwood.

Approve/deny? If approved I will coordinate legal redline and ask product ops to produce the activation checklist and estimated engineering effort.

-Marissa
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contingency activation latency & redundancy scope amendment — request for approval

Team — I reviewed Marissa's recommendation and approve a scoped, time-boxed amendment with the guardrails she proposed. Please proceed with these specific items: 

1) Legal: prepare a redline that amends the standard SLA to include a "Warm-Standby Activation" appendix limited to the payments-clearing namespace, with RTO = 120 minutes and RPO = 4 hours, term = 12 months pilot, automatic re-eval on renewal. Limit liability to one month's committed spend and require Nimbus to run quarterly DR tests.

2) Product Ops / SRE (Hannah): produce an activation checklist and a short-runbook appendix (<= 6 pages) that we will attach to the amendment. Add the required telemetry hooks (activation timestamp, region, and pre/post token counts) to the playbook. Estimate effort and let Marissa know if an onboarding fee is required.

3) Customer comms (Avery & Marissa): send Kelsey a one-page summary and the draft redline by EOD 17 Mar. Request a sign-off timeline from Nimbus by 24 Mar.

Thanks — good closing motion.

Aditya Rao
VP, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
